reason: §2190 sets the sabbath of the first creation against Sunday, which recalls the new creation inaugurated by the Resurrection. 'Replaced' is the In Brief form of §2175 ('Sunday fulfills the spiritual truth of the Jewish sabbath'), so preparatory holds, and Sacramental suits the Lord's Day as the Church's liturgical day.
§2259 reads the account of Abel's murder as revealing anger and envy as fruits of original sin. It is real teaching about Abel and Cain, with no type-antitype link in the paragraph.
§2542 teaches, with Rom 7, that the Law entrusted to Israel never sufficed to justify. This is teaching about the Law, with no figure-fulfilment wording.
§2569 presents Noah's pleasing offering and his 'walking with God' as prayer rooted in creation. Teaching only.

'Abraham's remarkable hospitality at Mamre foreshadows the annunciation of the true Son of the promise' is explicit wording, and both Types are rightly at event level. Christological is right because the text stresses the announced Son rather than Mary.

The link is real (the text echoes Rom 8:32, which itself echoes Gen 22:16), but the text says only that Abraham is 'conformed to the likeness of the Father'. That is a spiritual likeness ('Prayer restores man to God's likeness'), not figure or prefigure wording about the event, so the Isaac-to-Passion link is implied: synthesized, not explicit.
§2573 teaches Jacob's night wrestling, which tradition kept as a 'symbol of prayer as a battle of faith'. That is a symbol of prayer, not a New Testament antitype, so teaches-only is right.

'The prayer of Moses ... will be fulfilled in the one mediator ... Christ Jesus' is fulfilment wording, so preparatory is right. Moses, mediator of the Old Covenant, to Christ the one mediator is the right pair at person level.
§2575 calls the bush 'one of the primordial images of prayer'. The image is of prayer, not of a New Testament reality, so teaches-only is correct.
§2575 teaches how Moses learns to pray in his dialogue with God at his call. Teaching only.
§2576 presents Moses' face-to-face converse with God as the type of contemplative prayer (in the ordinary sense of 'model'). Teaching only.
§2577 teaches Moses' intercession 'in the breach' after the apostasy. It points forward only to later intercessors among the Jewish people and in the Church, not to Christ, so teaches-only fits.
§2578 teaches how Samuel learned prayer from Hannah and Eli, and the cost of his intercession. Teaching only.

'The prayer of Christ, the true Messiah and Son of David, will reveal and fulfill the meaning of this prayer' is fulfilment wording, and 'the prayer of God's Anointed' grounds David to Christ as a typological pair. It is not a prophecy row: what is fulfilled is David's prayer, not a prediction.
§2580 teaches Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the Temple. 'The king' in the quote is Solomon, named in the sentence before.
§2580 teaches the Temple as the house of prayer David wanted and Solomon built. There is no figure wording.
§2581 teaches the Temple as Israel's school of prayer. Its 'signs of the holiness and glory of God' point to prayer, not to a New Testament antitype.
§2582 teaches Elijah as 'father' of the prophets and a model of prayer. 'Foretells' stays inside the Old Testament (his name and the people's cry on Carmel), so it is not typology.

§696 calls the fire on the Carmel sacrifice a 'figure' of the Spirit's fire 'who transforms what he touches', and §2583 says the Eastern liturgies repeat Elijah's plea in the Eucharistic epiclesis, where the Spirit is invoked on the gifts. Together the link is clear and synthesized is the right label; Eucharist is the nearest existing antitype, the precise point being the epiclesis.

reason: §2583 joins Moses and Elijah hiding 'in a cleft of the rock' while God passes by, and says 'only on the mountain of the Transfiguration' will they behold the unveiled face they sought. The veiled theophany is completed in Christ, so preparatory fits even without the word 'fulfilled', and the event-level Types are right.
§2583 teaches Elijah's prayer at Zarephath and the raising of the widow's son. Teaching only.

§2584 teaches that the prophets' intercession 'awaits and prepares for the intervention of the Savior God'. The goal is God's saving action in general, not a named New Testament figure, so it is too general for a preparatory row.
'It foreshadows the prayer of intercession of the unique mediator, Christ Jesus' is explicit wording, and Moses to Christ is the right pair at person level.

§2598 uses Moses' approach to the bush (first contemplate, then hear) as the pattern for approaching Jesus' prayer. It is a simile about the approach, not a statement that the bush figures Christ, so teaches-only is the most the text supports.

'The new Eve, the true Mother of all the living' is a typological title with no prefigure or figure wording. 'True' marks Eve's title (Gen 3:20) as fulfilled in Mary, so the label is preparatory, not explicit.

'Mary ... is the daughter of Zion in person' names Mary as the personal realization of the personified Zion, with no figure or prefigure wording, so the label is preparatory. The Type is right: the personified people, not Zephaniah's oracle as a prediction.

Mary is called 'the ark of the covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells' as a title, with no prefigure or figure wording, so at most preparatory. The Type and the Marian category are right.

§2684 cites 'the spirit' of Elijah handed on 'to Elisha and John the Baptist' only as an analogy for how a founder's charism passes to his followers. Elisha's place in the same list shows the point is inheritance of a charism, not figure and fulfilment; if the Elijah-to-John link is wanted, §§717-720 is better ground.
§2777 reads the bush as the 'threshold of the divine holiness' that only Jesus could cross. That is a contrast with Moses, not a figure-fulfilment claim, so teaches-only fits.

The Promised Land is not named and there is no figure wording. The text calls heaven our homeland and says sin 'exiled us from the land of the covenant', borrowing Israel's land-and-exile language, so the link is implied by that borrowing: synthesized, not explicit.
'The new Eve ... preserved from sin and the corruption of death' is a typological title, with an implied contrast to Eve's fall, but no prefigure or figure wording, so at most preparatory.
Sound event-level Type, named in §2571's own words, and Gen 18:1-15 is the right text. Keeping it distinct from Abraham the person is correct, since the figure is the visit and its announcement.
An event-level antitype is the right precision for 'the annunciation of the true Son of the promise', and the description (Luke 1:26-38) is accurate.
Sound event-level Type: §2583 names 'the mountain of the Transfiguration', and the description (Matt 17:1-8) is accurate.
